svg.text: Built with Next.js, Node.js, SQL, AWS, CDN, Docker, Kubernetes and Redis — follow one request through 5 stages
Each stage = one layer a request passes through. Steps are numbered (1.1, 1.2 …).
In simple words: what the visitor touches. A pre-built Next.js page is delivered by the CDN, with optimized photos, behind a firewall.
• Build assets are pushed to S3
Gives nested layouts, Server Components by default, loading.tsx streaming and the Metadata API. Static build today; later a Docker image.
In simple words: one front door to the cluster. It checks login (JWT), limits abuse with Redis and sends each request to the right Node.js service.
In simple words: the brains. Each job is a small Node.js (Express) service in a Docker container, run by Kubernetes so each can scale alone.
In simple words: where data is kept (SQL), remembered fast (Redis), stored as files (S3) and processed later (job queue).
In simple words: how code is packed into containers, shipped automatically, scaled with traffic and watched for problems.
Example: one visit from start to finish
Stage 1 is built today. Stages 2–5 are the target architecture for a future full-scale build, not yet implemented.
